findings.title: website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous website hiding
findings.body: website_name is computed from the profile website and added as a public attribute, but it is not registered in untrusted_attributes, which is what suppresses website for anonymous viewers of trust-level 0 users. include_website_name also never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?. Previously the profile label was derived in the browser from model.website, so omitting website also omitted the label. After this change, an anonymous GET of a TL0 user still receives website_name (the hostname, and host plus path when the same-domain branch matches) even though website is withheld. That discloses the URL the serializer is supposed to hide; with the path appended, the withheld URL can be reconstructed. The profile template will render that text. The spec's TL0 example still only asserts that website is absent and never checks website_name, so the regression is untested. Adding the missing ? on the include hook is not enough: that method only checks website.present?, which is true in this case.

findings.title: include_website_name is never called
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers includes an attribute only if include_<name>? returns true. Every other hook in this serializer uses that form (include_email?, include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, and the methods defined by untrusted_attributes). include_website_name has no question mark, so it is never invoked and the website.present? guard is dead code. website_name is therefore always serialized, including a null website_name when the user has no website or the host cannot be parsed. The omission the new method was written to provide cannot happen.

findings.title: Same-domain check mismatches common hosts
findings.body: The decision to append the URL path does not compare registrable domains, so it both over-matches and under-matches. The elsif treats hosts as the same site when they have the same label count greater than 2 and share every label after the first. That equates unrelated sites that only share a public suffix: a forum at forum.co.uk and a website of http://phishing.co.uk/login both reduce to co.uk, so the profile shows phishing.co.uk/login instead of phishing.co.uk. The same false positive applies to *.com.au, *.co.jp, *.blogspot.com, *.github.io, and similar. The else branch only checks discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host), so the path is added when the website is a parent of the forum, but not when the website is a subdomain of the forum. A forum at example.com with website http://www.example.com/docs or http://blog.example.com/users/jane displays only www.example.com or blog.example.com, which hides the path this change is meant to show. Comparison is also case-sensitive: URI#host is lowercased, but Discourse.current_hostname is not normalized here, so a mixed-case hostname fails the exact-match branch and drops the path. The new specs only cover an unrelated host, an exact match, and the website-is-parent direction; they never exercise the elsif or the www/subdomain cases.

findings.title: Non-ASCII website URLs vanish from the profile
findings.body: The host is parsed with URI(...).host rescue nil, and a nil host makes website_name return nil. The profile template now shows the globe and link only when model.website_name is present, with no fallback to model.website. Ruby's stdlib URI raises URI::InvalidURIError on non-ASCII input (for example http://例え.jp/path) and on URLs containing spaces; those errors are swallowed, so website_name is null and the link disappears even though website is still stored and is still serialized for viewers allowed to see it. The old client label used website.split("/")[2], which still displayed a hostname for those strings. Internationalized profile websites that previously appeared are now omitted until rewritten as ASCII or punycode.

findings.title: Website label goes stale after website changes
findings.body: The header used to label the site with a controller computed property that observed model.website and updated when the website changed. It now renders the server field model.website_name, which is copied onto the model only when the user payload is first loaded. User#save sends the new website but only copies bio_excerpt back from the PUT response, so it never refreshes website_name. The header lives in user.hbs outside {{outlet}} and stays visible on preferences and other child routes. After model.website changes, the anchor href is the new URL while the link text is still the previous website_name until a full reload, so the visible label can name a different host than the link destination.
